The likely reaction is a **Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling**, replacing the aryl iodide C–I bond with the aryl group from the organoboron reagent:

**Product:** the biaryl linking the quinoline-derived aryl fragment to the methyl-substituted fused N-heteroaryl fragment.

### Comparison

| Organoboron reagent | Relevant empirical result | Yield |
|---|---|---:|
| **Pinacol boronic ester** `...c1B1OC(C)(C)C(C)(C)O1` | Exact aryl iodide pair; KOH, acetonitrile, bulky Pd/phosphine catalyst; 100 °C, 1 h | **99.0%** |
| **Potassium aryltrifluoroborate** `...c1[B-](F)(F)F.[K+]` | Same coupling product observed, but records used fluoride/base systems rather than the specified KOH/acetonitrile combination | **83.1–84.8%** |

### Optimal choice

Use the **pinacol boronic ester**. It has direct empirical support under the requested conditions—**KOH in acetonitrile with a bulky phosphine/Pd catalyst**, giving approximately **99% yield at 100 °C for 1 hour** (reaction record `ord-8e3f8ca837f44a47b9ff648e461d1213`, tool call `call_oQkb70rKNaN6MRXaU90Rwt0R`).

The potassium aryltrifluoroborate is also a viable Suzuki partner and gives the same biaryl product, but the retrieved examples give lower yields, about **83–85%**, and do not directly reproduce the specified KOH/acetonitrile conditions (tool call `call_BY3dIJW8W4zl7ltCZeUTzG2q`).
